text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Centre-left United Democrats leader George Vassiliou accuses Communist Akel of breaching ethics for divulging contents of private conversations between leaders of the two parties. Three-party alliance to contest next year's presidential elections collapses over weekend.
- Authorities draw up tighter regulations on use of speedboats after recent accidents.
- Akel leader Demetris Christofias expresses reservations at chances of achieving breakthrough on Cyprus problem at next round of U.N.-sponsored talks in Switzerland.
- Former Foreign Minister George Iakovou may announce this week his bid for presidency.

- Varying interpretations given to threat of Turkish side in not going to next round of U.N.-sponsored talks. Turkish Cypriot leader Denktash has threatened not to take part but leaves final decision open until his parliament convenes this week.
- Justice Minister Nicos Koshis vows to nip organised crime in bud. Police have valid suspicions gangland figures also have associates in Turkish-occupied areas.
